query: For a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix evaluated in sliding from room temperature to 800 °C, what single intervention could overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range? Earlier studies of other self-lubricating material systems reported low coefficients of friction at 704 °C and favorable friction and wear behavior over broad temperature ranges. However, these results do not resolve the limited understanding of wide-temperature tribological performance in CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys, and effectiveness must be maintained as operating temperature, load, and environment vary. Formulate one hypothesis that identifies a single intervention without presupposing its class, explains its mechanism, predicts friction and wear relative to the starting CoCrFeNi material, defines its temperature, load, and environmental boundaries, relates it to prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Incorporation of 15 vol% CaF2 micro-particles into a CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy matrix will form a continuous, load-activated CaF2 tribofilm during sliding, maintaining a coefficient of friction below 0.3 and reducing wear rate by at least 50% relative to the unmodified CoCrFeNi across 25 – 800 °C under loads up to 20 N in both air and inert environments.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy (grain size ≈20 µm, hardness ≈200 HV), no solid-lubricant phases present.
generation.intervention: Powder-metallurgy blending of 15 vol% CaF2 micro-particles with CoCrFeNi powder, followed by hot pressing at 1000 °C and annealing for 2 h to produce a uniform composite.
generation.conditions: Pin-on-disk sliding against alumina counterface, temperatures stepped from 25 to 800 °C, normal loads of 1, 10, and 20 N, sliding speed 10 mm/s, environments: laboratory air and Ar.
generation.structural_mediator: A continuous CaF2-rich tribofilm at the sliding interface.
generation.mechanism: Under contact stress and thermal activation, CaF2 particles extrude and plastically deform at the surface, generating a low-shear-strength fluoride layer stable up to 800 °C, which decouples metal–metal asperity contact and lowers friction and wear.
generation.predicted_outcome: Coefficient of friction remains <0.3 and wear rate remains <5×10^-6 mm^3/Nm throughout 25–800 °C, representing ≥50% reduction compared to unmodified CoCrFeNi.
generation.baseline: Unmodified CoCrFeNi exhibits μ≈0.6 at RT rising to ≈0.8 at 800 °C and wear rate ≈1×10^-5 mm^3/Nm under similar test conditions.
generation.boundary: Valid for temperatures 25–800 °C, loads 1–20 N, sliding speed 10 mm/s, durations up to 30 min, in air or Ar.
generation.uncertainty: Above ~700 °C in air, CaF2 oxidation may degrade tribofilm; predicted friction and wear values are approximate (±0.05 μ, ±20% wear rate).

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate CoCrFeNi-15 vol% CaF2 composite disks by powder metallurgy. Perform pin-on-disk tests with alumina ball at 10 mm/s, steps of 25, 200, 400, 600, and 800 °C in air and Ar, under 1, 10, and 20 N for 30 min each.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Hypothesis is falsified if μ exceeds 0.5 or wear rate exceeds 1×10^-5 mm^3/Nm at any tested temperature or load.
